summary.headline: HOEC Q2 FY27 revenue rose 25% QoQ to INR147 crore and EBITDA more than doubled to INR46 crore, helped by one-time B-80 HPCL crude realisation.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 recovery was driven by gas sales growth and realisation of previous-year B-80 HPCL crude inventory, with consolidated revenue of INR151.78 crore, EBITDA of INR37.51 crore (24.71% margin) and PAT of INR19.03 crore. Management reiterated an 11,000 boe/d operating target by mid-2027 and set a 10,000 boe/d net target by June 2027, with 22,000 boe/d in FY28 and 30,000-32,000 boe/d by FY29. Dirok gas output rose to about 0.7 mmscmd gross from 0.4-0.5 earlier, with pipeline debottlenecking (DNPL/NRL) the gating item. B-80 remains offline for workovers and drilling, with the rig expected late November or early December. The company raised INR125 crore of loans for the workovers and holds about 36,104 t of B-80 inventory still to be monetised.

financial_highlights.change: Revenue from operations up 25% QoQ from INR117 crore (per CFO's standalone-style figure of INR147 crore)
More than doubled from INR21 crore in Q1 (CFO cited INR46 crore on a separate basis)
Tripled from INR12.5 crore in Q1

Adjusted PAT up 46% from INR34.73 crore, after excluding a one-time INR32.5 crore B-80 investment restatement in H1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR57.79 crore in Q2; close to INR80 crore cumulative in H1 FY27
INR18.23 crore (CFO also cited INR39 crore operational cash surplus)

segments.name: B-80 (offshore Bombay High)
segments.commentary: Two subsea wells (D1, D2); D2 has watered out at 93-94%. Workover targets 1,000-1,500 bopd plus 5-7 mmscfd gas, with on-stream expected end-December/early January. Three new wells to follow, with drilling finished by 15 May. Company margin guided at USD30-40/boe; opex USD20-30/boe.

segments.name: Dirok (Assam)
segments.commentary: Gross gas output rose to about 0.7 mmscmd from 0.4-0.5 earlier; capacity is 1.2 mmscmd. Realisation is linked to the PPAC price, about USD7.5-7.8/MMBtu in August and about USD12 currently. Output is evacuation-constrained until the DNPL line is restored to 90 bar, which could lift output to about 2.5 mmscmd.

segments.name: Kharsang (Assam)
segments.commentary: Oil production has doubled; target is 1,200-1,400 bopd from 680-700 bopd after nine more wells, starting January/February. Two gas wells with 8-9 mmscfd potential are shut in pending a 24 km pipeline (about 18 months).

segments.name: PY-1 (Cauvery)
segments.commentary: Gas field shut for an extended period after GAIL halted offtake. PetroVietnam assessment indicates 15-20 mmscfd potential. Coiled tubing intervention with SLB has slipped past monsoon. New drilling depends on a firm take-or-pay contract with IOCL or GAIL, with rented compressors needed.

segments.name: Cambay (Gujarat)
segments.commentary: Palej production doubled. Asjol needs two wells and North Balol needs sucker rod pumps. Partnering with GSPC and seeking third-party EOR.

segments.name: B-174 and B-15
segments.commentary: B-174 added in 2026 with about 800 sq km of acreage in total; 8 locations, 5-6 material discoveries. B-15 is targeted for development from Q4 FY28 with first oil in June 2028, adding 3,000-3,500 boe/d.

guidance_outlook: Net production of about 10,000 boe/d by June 2027 (range 8,500-11,000); 11,000 boe/d operating target by mid-2027 unchanged.
FY28 target of about 22,000 boe/d with B-15 online; 30,000-32,000 boe/d net by FY29 after B-174.
B-80 workover on-stream by end-December/early January, with a 15-day delay to Q3 from late rig mobilisation. B-80 drilling to finish by 15 May 2027.
Dirok gas capacity can rise to 2.5 mmscmd once DNPL/NRL work is done, targeted by mid-December to end-December 2026, with the Dirok bottleneck removed.
Cash inflows from B-80 and HPCL crude estimated at about INR250 crore; banking lines of up to INR600-700 crore being sought, total up to INR1,000 crore.
capex_capacity: B-80: wells USD45 million and workover USD15 million (total about USD60 million per management; an analyst cited USD65 million). Rig for workover and drilling awarded; tubulars and integrated services contracts let.

PY-1: intervention via SLB, with 2 new wells costing USD20-25 million each to be drilled only after a firm take-or-pay contract. Rented compressors needed to lift pressure from 10 bar to 63 bar at the IOCL station, 24 km away.
Kharsang: 9 wells approved; drilling from January/February 2027. Two deep wells planned for Q3 FY28.
Dirok: 2 more wells approved by DGH, which would lift capacity from 1.2 to 2.0 mmscmd, but these will be drilled only after debottlenecking.
B-174 development from October 2028 (B-80 drilling from October 2027). Development may need one or more facilities or tie-backs to ONGC infrastructure.
demand_pricing: Dirok gas realisation is linked to PPAC pricing and was about USD7.8/MMBtu in August, about USD12/MMBtu currently; management expects USD9-11 on average once the national grid link is in place.
Gas off-take at Dirok is mainly Oil India (rich gas); AGCL (about 20% of gas) is price-sensitive. Management expects a 10-20% volume impact once NRL becomes a reseller.
Asian spot LNG averaged about USD21.5/MMBtu (March-October) per IEA; domestic gas prices are not following this.

B-80 crude: HPCL dispute over quality, with 417,000 barrels (INR260 crore) sold; arbitration deferred and lifting resumed. Around 120,000-130,000 barrels remain in the FSO. Replacement tanker and dry-docking needed. Future samples are being tested for quality, and IOCL is reviewing them for lifting.
Each USD10/bbl increase in oil price adds about INR30-40 crore to B-80 revenue; profit petroleum adds variability.

qa_highlights.question: Margin range by asset (Dirok, Kharsang, PY-1, B-80) at about USD70 crude, and how monsoon disruption risk is handled at B-80.
qa_highlights.answer: B-80 margins guided at USD30-40/boe on a company basis, with opex USD20-30/boe; each USD10/bbl oil price move adds about INR30-40 crore to B-80 revenue. Monsoon risk: a small MOPU buffer of 2-3 days of production, rig demobilised by 15 May, and subsea/SPM design review next year.

qa_highlights.question: Volume guidance for H2 FY27 and FY28, gross or net.
qa_highlights.answer: About 10,000 boe/d net HOEC by June 2027 (range 8,500-11,000), 22,000 boe/d in FY28 after B-15 (3,000-3,500 boe/d, first oil June 2028), and 30,000-32,000 boe/d by FY29 after B-174.

qa_highlights.question: Dirok gas volumes rose to about 22 mmscfd from 14-15; is this sustainable and what is the realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the run rate is sustainable. Realisation is PPAC-linked, about USD7.78 in August and about USD12/MMBtu currently; Oil India takes the rich gas, while AGCL (about 20% of gas) is price-sensitive, with a 10-20% volume impact expected once NRL becomes a reseller.

qa_highlights.question: Status of DNPL pipeline upgrade and the timeline for grid connectivity.
qa_highlights.answer: Hot tapping was dropped in favour of an NRL bypass line to the national grid; spur-line material was delivered in early October. Grid connection is still targeted for December end, with a best case mid-December; Dirok capacity could then rise from 1.2 to 2.5 mmscmd at 90 bar.

qa_highlights.question: Is PY-1 drilling likely next year, and what is the gas offtake route?
qa_highlights.answer: No contract is awarded until a take-or-pay or heads of agreement with IOCL or GAIL is signed; management gives P50 odds for a signed take-or-pay next year. Rented compressors are needed to lift pressure from 10 bar to 63 bar at the IOCL station 24 km away. Two wells cost USD20-25 million each.

qa_highlights.question: Why has B-80 capex moved from USD45 million to USD65 million?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said wells are USD45 million and workover USD15 million, so the total is USD60 million, unchanged from last quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Kharsang oil targets after the next nine wells, and B-174 development timing and facilities.
qa_highlights.answer: Kharsang oil is about 680-700 bopd now, targeted at 1,200-1,400 bopd. B-174 development starts October 2028 and takes about two years; it may need one or more facilities or tie-backs to ONGC, with 2P reserves at 21 million boe per DGH.

qa_highlights.question: Steps to avoid a repeat of the HPCL quality dispute, and whether equity will be raised for capex.
qa_highlights.answer: Samples are tested regularly, with third-party testing planned and IOCL reviewing samples; D1 and D2 are said to show nil light content. On funding, management said project-level partners for PY-1 are possible, but no HOEC-level equity is planned; bank lines of INR600-700 crore are being sought.

risks_watch: B-80 workover timing: rig arrives end-November or early December, and a 15-day slip to Q3 is already flagged. On-stream is targeted for end-December or early January.
Dirok evacuation: output stays capped until the DNPL/NRL line is restored to 90 bar, targeted for mid-December to end-December 2026. Any slip delays the 2.5 mmscmd step-up.

Gas price exposure: AGCL is price-sensitive, with a 10-20% volume impact expected once NRL becomes a reseller. Realisation depends on the monthly PPAC price, which moved from about USD7.8 to about USD12/MMBtu.

B-80 crude monetisation: about 120,000-130,000 barrels remain in the FSO and about 36,104 t of inventory is still to be sold. Lifting awaits a replacement tanker and dry-docking, and HPCL quality issues remain unresolved.

Funding for the peak capex over the next 3-4 months: INR125 crore of loans raised, with banking lines of INR600-700 crore being sought, and cash inflows of about INR250 crore targeted. PY-1 drilling depends on a firm take-or-pay contract that is not yet signed.

summary.management_tone: Confident on the B-80 workover, Dirok debottlenecking and the 10,000 boe/d June 2027 target, but cautious on PY-1 (drilling conditional on a firm take-or-pay), on grid timelines outside management's control, and on monetising B-80 crude. Management repeatedly hedged the margin and EBITDA questions as highly variable and declined to give a precise EBITDA figure.
